:::{#cor-uncorrelated-cor-zero}
#### Uncorrelated means zero correlation

If $X$ and $Y$ have finite, positive [variances](#def-variance),
then $X$ and $Y$ are [uncorrelated](#def-uncorrelated)
[if and only if](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-iff) $\Cor{X,Y} = 0$.

:::

::: proof

By @def-correlation, $\Cor{X,Y} = \Cov{X,Y} / \paren{\SD{X}\,\SD{Y}}$,
and $\SD{X}\,\SD{Y} > 0$ because both [variances](#def-variance) are positive, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
so $\Cor{X,Y} = 0$ [if and only if](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-iff) $\Cov{X,Y} = 0$,
which is @def-uncorrelated.

:::
